Adopt SI units and the following model-local quantity roles. Here the selected Einstein–Maxwell framework combines the stated Lorentzian geometry with a classical electromagnetic two-form and current; this definition itself supplies no gravitational equation, matter action, or empirical claim. A primitive is an input or independent field variable of this formulation; a derived quantity is fixed by a stated construction from its inputs. Neither label is universal across physical theories, and unit choice alone does not determine it.

The spacetime data are a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless four-manifold $M$, a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a smooth time-orientation field, and an independent orientation, exactly as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The metric, its time orientation, and the manifold orientation are separate data. An observer at $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth observer congruence is a smooth field of such vectors. A local tetrad is a smooth basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; an observer congruence, a coordinate chart, and a tetrad are different objects. Tetrads and observer fields need only exist locally; this definition assumes no global inertial chart, global tetrad, or hypersurface-orthogonal congruence.

The electromagnetic field-strength variable $F$ is a smooth real two-form, hence an alternating covariant tensor of type $(0,2)$, on an open subset of $M$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. It is primitive in this formulation. For an observer congruence $n$, its electric and magnetic observer covectors are derived by

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $\star_g$ is the unique Hodge map characterized pointwise by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, using the metric and independent orientation, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Both covectors annihilate $n$ and lie in the rest covector space $\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n)=0\}$, whose induced metric is positive definite. In a positively oriented future orthonormal tetrad with $e_0=n$ and $\epsilon_{123}=+1$, their spatial components obey the fixed dictionary $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ from [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. Thus $E$ and $B$ are observer-dependent derived fields, not globally defined observer-independent three-vectors on a curved spacetime. Their tetrad components have units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and tesla (T), respectively; the components of $F$ in a length-coordinate chart have unit T. No global potential is assumed; when a local potential $A_a$ is used, its components have unit $\mathrm{T\,m}$ and a scalar potential $\varphi$ has unit V.

For any chosen observer $n$, a smooth four-current is a vector field $j$ whose local decomposition is $j=c\rho\,n+J$, where $\rho:=-g(n,j)/c$ is the observer charge density and $J:=j-c\rho n$ is orthogonal to $n$. In the associated positively oriented orthonormal tetrad its components are $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The units are $[\rho]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[J^i]=[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[q]=\mathrm C$ for a charge parameter supplied by a matter model. The current is a prescribed input or is supplied by an explicitly stated matter model; it is not inferred from the Maxwell equation alone.

The SI constants and coordinate units are fixed as follows. The speed of ideal vacuum light $c>0$ is the exact SI defining constant $299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; identifying it with the shared ideal-light and clock conversion constant is the adopted Minkowski model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], not a consequence of its unit definition. The elementary charge $e$ is exactly $1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$. These unit definitions do not imply that charge is quantized. The magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ has unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined in the revised SI, so no exact numerical value for $\mu_0$ is adopted. Define the electric constant (vacuum permittivity) $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$; hence $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$, and $\varepsilon_0$ has the same relative standard uncertainty as $\mu_0$ because $c$ is exact. The exact component equation $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ is dimensionally consistent: both sides have unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$ in a length-coordinate frame.

In a length-coordinate chart all four coordinate values are assigned metres, with $x^0=ct$ when a time coordinate $t$ in seconds is selected. This is local coordinate bookkeeping, not a global inertial-coordinate claim. In such a chart $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless, the Levi-Civita coefficients $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and curvature components have unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Components in other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

The coupling normalization $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ is derived from these parameters and has unit $\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$. This definition records the convention for a later Einstein equation; it asserts no Einstein equation. A separate positive normalization $\kappa_0$ with unit weber (Wb) is a chosen flux conversion reserved for a later explicitly specified $U(1)$ formulation, where $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ under multiplication. It is not $\kappa_E$, an electric charge, $\mu_0$, or Planck's constant, and it implies no charge quantization. Test-particle rest mass $m>0$ in kg and charge $q$ in C are externally supplied matter parameters, not quantities derived by classical electromagnetism.

These are SI and model-definition conventions only. They neither assert empirical measurements beyond the stated SI defining constants and measured status of $\mu_0$, nor identify similarly named quantities in another framework.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, let $\mathcal X$ be a set, and let

$$S:\mathcal D\longrightarrow\mathbb R$$

be a real-valued functional defined on a subset $\mathcal D$ of the set of
pairs $(\tilde g,\varphi)$ with $\tilde g$ a smooth Lorentzian metric on $M$ of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $\varphi\in\mathcal X$. Fix $(\tilde g,\varphi)\in
\mathcal D$; below we always take $\tilde g=g$. The elements $\varphi$ are the
model's matter configurations; nothing about their nature is assumed here.
Assume that $\mathcal D$ admits every compactly supported metric direction at
$(g,\varphi)$: for each smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $h$ with
compact support, there is $\varepsilon_h>0$ such that
$(g+s h,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon_h$. Since
$\mathcal D$ contains only pairs whose metric is Lorentzian, these admitted
linear families are Lorentzian throughout that interval. This condition makes every compactly
supported inverse-metric variation available as well, since
$h\mapsto -g^{ac}g^{bd}h_{cd}$ is a bijection on compactly supported smooth
symmetric tensor fields.

**(a) Metric families.** A **smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly
supported variation** is a map $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<\varepsilon$ for some
$\varepsilon>0$, such that $(g_s,\varphi)\in\mathcal D$ for all $s$, such that
$g_s$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ for every $s$,
such that in every chart $(U,x)$ the component functions
$(s,x(p))\mapsto (g_s)_{ab}(p)$ are jointly $C^\infty$ on
$(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times x(U)$,
such that $g_0=g$, and such that there is a compact subset $K\subseteq M$ with
$g_s=g$ outside $K$ for every $|s|<\varepsilon$. For such a family define

$$q^{ab}:=\frac{d}{ds}g_s^{ab}\Big|_{s=0},$$

the derivative at $s=0$ of the components of the inverse metric of $g_s$ in any
smooth chart; the family of functions $q^{ab}$ is a smooth symmetric
contravariant $2$-tensor field of compact support, well defined because the
components $g_s^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $s$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

**(b) Hilbert tensor.** A smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on
$M$ is a **Hilbert stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to
$c$** when, for **every** smooth metric family $s\mapsto g_s$ at $g$ with
compactly supported variation,

$$\frac{d}{ds}S(g_s,\varphi)\Big|_{s=0}=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\, \mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $\mathrm{vol}_g$ is the metric volume form of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and $\int_M\omega$ is the
integral of the compactly supported smooth top form $\omega:=T_{ab}q^{ab}
\mathrm{vol}_g$ over the oriented manifold $M$
([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]).
The right-hand side is defined because $q^{ab}$ has compact support, so
$\omega$ is compactly supported. If such a $T$ exists it is unique, by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]]; one then calls it **the** Hilbert
stress-energy tensor of $S$ at $(g,\varphi)$.

**(c) Conventions and scope.** The sign and the factor $1/(2c)$ are fixed
conventions of this library: they are the ones that turn the framework's
adopted Einstein-Hilbert normalization into the field equation displayed in the
framework's physical postulate. The condition is a property of the functional
$S$ at the point $(g,\varphi)$; it is not automatic, and this definition does
not assert that any functional has a Hilbert tensor. The definition uses the
orientation of $M$; a general functional $S$ has no orientation-reversal law,
so no transformation of $S$ or $T$ is asserted. When $S$ is given by
integrating $L(g,\varphi)\mathrm{vol}_g$ with an orientation-independent
scalar coefficient $L$ and the integral exists (or compact action differences
are used), define the reversed-orientation action by the same construction.
Reversing orientation replaces $\mathrm{vol}_g$ by $-\mathrm{vol}_g$ and
reverses the sign of integration of a fixed top form. These two signs cancel,
so both the action variation and the integral in the defining identity are
unchanged, as is its tensor $T$.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with metric-selected connection $\nabla$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth principal $U(1)$ bundle with a smooth connection and global curvature two-form $F$, using the local-potential and fixed-sector conventions of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]] and [[lem-emg-circle-connection-gluing]]. Let $\Psi$ be a smooth matter configuration and let $S_m$ be a real differentiable functional of $(g,A,\Psi)$, where $A$ denotes the bundle connection, not necessarily a global one-form.

Fix a configuration at which the matter Euler–Lagrange variation vanishes, meaning $\delta_\Psi S_m=0$ for every smooth compactly supported matter-field variation. Suppose that for all compactly supported metric variations $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$ and all compactly supported connection variations $\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$ in the fixed bundle sector, the remaining first variation is

$$\delta S_m=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T^m_{ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+\frac{1}{c}\int_M j^a\alpha_a\,\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $c>0$, $T^m$ is a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and $j$ is a smooth vector field. Assume $S_m$ is invariant under compactly supported gauge transformations and under simultaneous pullback along the local flow of every compactly supported smooth vector field, with the connection and matter field transported by the induced horizontal lift to $P$. Only the local variations at flow parameter $s=0$ are used. Then

$$\nabla_a j^a=0,\qquad \nabla_a T_m^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c,$$

where $j_c:=g_{ca}j^a$. These are conditional variational identities; no Maxwell or Einstein field equation, existence theorem, or empirical premise is assumed.

For SI bookkeeping in length coordinates, take $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-1}}$, and $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$. If $S_m$ is assigned action units $\mathrm{J\,s}$, the displayed variation convention assigns $[T^m]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ and $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. These are formal dimensional assignments only; the lemma adopts no matter model or empirical law.

Adopt SI units and the following model-local quantity roles. Here the selected Einstein–Maxwell framework combines the stated Lorentzian geometry with a classical electromagnetic two-form and current; this definition itself supplies no gravitational equation, matter action, or empirical claim. A primitive is an input or independent field variable of this formulation; a derived quantity is fixed by a stated construction from its inputs. Neither label is universal across physical theories, and unit choice alone does not determine it.

The spacetime data are a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless four-manifold $M$, a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a smooth time-orientation field, and an independent orientation, exactly as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The metric, its time orientation, and the manifold orientation are separate data. An observer at $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth observer congruence is a smooth field of such vectors. A local tetrad is a smooth basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; an observer congruence, a coordinate chart, and a tetrad are different objects. Tetrads and observer fields need only exist locally; this definition assumes no global inertial chart, global tetrad, or hypersurface-orthogonal congruence.

The electromagnetic field-strength variable $F$ is a smooth real two-form, hence an alternating covariant tensor of type $(0,2)$, on an open subset of $M$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. It is primitive in this formulation. For an observer congruence $n$, its electric and magnetic observer covectors are derived by

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $\star_g$ is the unique Hodge map characterized pointwise by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, using the metric and independent orientation, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Both covectors annihilate $n$ and lie in the rest covector space $\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n)=0\}$, whose induced metric is positive definite. In a positively oriented future orthonormal tetrad with $e_0=n$ and $\epsilon_{123}=+1$, their spatial components obey the fixed dictionary $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ from [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. Thus $E$ and $B$ are observer-dependent derived fields, not globally defined observer-independent three-vectors on a curved spacetime. Their tetrad components have units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and tesla (T), respectively; the components of $F$ in a length-coordinate chart have unit T. No global potential is assumed; when a local potential $A_a$ is used, its components have unit $\mathrm{T\,m}$ and a scalar potential $\varphi$ has unit V.

For any chosen observer $n$, a smooth four-current is a vector field $j$ whose local decomposition is $j=c\rho\,n+J$, where $\rho:=-g(n,j)/c$ is the observer charge density and $J:=j-c\rho n$ is orthogonal to $n$. In the associated positively oriented orthonormal tetrad its components are $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The units are $[\rho]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[J^i]=[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[q]=\mathrm C$ for a charge parameter supplied by a matter model. The current is a prescribed input or is supplied by an explicitly stated matter model; it is not inferred from the Maxwell equation alone.

The SI constants and coordinate units are fixed as follows. The speed of ideal vacuum light $c>0$ is the exact SI defining constant $299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; identifying it with the shared ideal-light and clock conversion constant is the adopted Minkowski model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], not a consequence of its unit definition. The elementary charge $e$ is exactly $1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$. These unit definitions do not imply that charge is quantized. The magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ has unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined in the revised SI, so no exact numerical value for $\mu_0$ is adopted. Define the electric constant (vacuum permittivity) $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$; hence $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$, and $\varepsilon_0$ has the same relative standard uncertainty as $\mu_0$ because $c$ is exact. The exact component equation $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ is dimensionally consistent: both sides have unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$ in a length-coordinate frame.

In a length-coordinate chart all four coordinate values are assigned metres, with $x^0=ct$ when a time coordinate $t$ in seconds is selected. This is local coordinate bookkeeping, not a global inertial-coordinate claim. In such a chart $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless, the Levi-Civita coefficients $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and curvature components have unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Components in other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

For the gravitational sector, take Newton's gravitational constant $G_N>0$ with unit $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$ and the cosmological constant parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ with unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ as primitive parameters of the selected model; no numerical value for either is used here. The coupling normalization $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ is derived from these parameters and has unit $\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$. This definition records the convention for a later Einstein equation; it asserts no Einstein equation. A separate positive normalization $\kappa_0$ with unit weber (Wb) is a chosen flux conversion reserved for a later explicitly specified $U(1)$ formulation, where $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ under multiplication. It is not $\kappa_E$, an electric charge, $\mu_0$, or Planck's constant, and it implies no charge quantization. Test-particle rest mass $m>0$ in kg and charge $q$ in C are externally supplied matter parameters, not quantities derived by classical electromagnetism.

These are SI and model-definition conventions only. They neither assert empirical measurements beyond the stated SI defining constants and measured status of $\mu_0$, nor identify similarly named quantities in another framework.

A smooth real $k$-form is a smooth section of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, and its space is denoted $\Omega^k(M)$, as in [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. In this page, $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ means an arbitrary smooth real two-form. No equation such as $dF=0$, no global potential, and no physical field law is included in this definition.

An **observer at $p\in M$** is a vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $g_p(n,N_p)<0$; its **rest space** is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. A smooth **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth vector field whose value at every point is an observer. Its observer curves are the maximal integral curves, and a chart is adapted to it when its three spatial coordinate functions are constant along those curves, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]. Such a congruence need not be hypersurface-orthogonal.

A **local frame field** on $U$ is an ordered smooth basis field of $TM|_U$. A **coordinate frame** is the basis of coordinate vector fields supplied by a chart. For every observer congruence $n$, each point has a neighborhood carrying an $n$-adapted tetrad; this is a local assertion only.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. For a compactly supported metric variation, write $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$, $h_{ab}=\delta g_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$, $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$, and $V^a=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^a{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^d{}_{db}$, where $\delta\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\frac12g^{ad}(\nabla_bh_{cd}+\nabla_ch_{bd}-\nabla_dh_{bc})$; curvature and Einstein tensors are as in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. The local density identity is

$$\delta((R-2\Lambda)w)=w(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab})q^{ab}+\partial_a(wV^a).$$

Fix constants $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Regard these as formal coefficients; their physical interpretation and units are not assumptions of this mathematical lemma. For smooth metric variations with compact support in the interior, at fixed bundle connection and fixed matter fields, consider the action difference

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(R-2\Lambda)\,\mathrm{vol}_g-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}\int_MF_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+S_m,$$

where noncompact action values are used only through compactly supported differences, $F$ is the curvature of a fixed smooth bundle connection, and $S_m$ has Hilbert tensor $T^m$ in the convention of [[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]. Let $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ be the electromagnetic Hilbert tensor supplied by the compact Maxwell variation of [[lem-emg-maxwell-action-variation]], and set $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. Then for every compactly supported inverse-metric variation $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$,

$$\delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M\left(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})\right)q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently, stationarity under all such metric variations is equivalent to

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}).$$

Any tensor fields satisfying this equation necessarily have $\nabla^a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})=0$ because $\Lambda$ is constant. This is a compatibility condition, not a claim that the coupled field equations have a solution or that matter and Maxwell equations follow from metric stationarity.

For dimensional bookkeeping in length coordinates one may assign $[R]=[\Lambda]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[G_N]=\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $[\mu_0]=\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, and $[T^m]=[T^{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. Then every action term has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$ and $\kappa_E T$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. These are formal assignments only; the lemma assumes no measured parameter value or physical field law.

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{EM}}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}F_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{2\mu_0c}F\wedge\star_gF.$$

When this density has a global integral, denote it by $S_{\mathrm{EM}}[g,F]$.
On a noncompact domain, every displayed variation below means the finite
action difference supported by the compactly supported variation.

Assume the fixed smooth bundle sector and connection-variation interface in
[A1] below. Then:

**(a) Connection variation.** For every smooth compactly supported global
one-form $\alpha$ allowed by that fixed-sector interface, holding $g$ fixed gives $\delta F=d\alpha$ and

$$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{EM}}[\alpha]=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_M(\nabla_aF^{ab})\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{m}}[\alpha]=c^{-1}\int_Mj^b\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g$ for a
smooth vector field $j$, then stationarity of
$S_{\mathrm{EM}}+S_{\mathrm m}$ under every such $\alpha$ is equivalent on $M$ to

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,$$

and hence to $d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. This is a conditional variational
calculation; it asserts no matter-action existence or physical adoption.

metric variation $q^{ab}:=\delta g^{ab}$, holding the lower components
$F_{ab}$ fixed and preserving Lorentz signature for sufficiently small
parameter, define $T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}$ by

$$\delta_gS_{\mathrm{EM}}[q]=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Then

$$T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

This is the tensor obtained by varying the free electromagnetic action; it
contains no stress contribution from a source or matter functional.

Adopt as a physical formulation principle of this framework, as an alternative
to postulating the field equations and the force law directly, the following
assumption about the functionals, variation classes and stationarity predicate
of [[def-em-field-action-definition]].

(i) [Field sector] A smooth field $A:N\to\mathbb R^4$ on the region $U$ of
clause (a) of that definition is dynamically admissible exactly when it is
stationary for the field action $S[A]$ under all compactly supported smooth
variations $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ in the sense of clause (b) of that
definition: $\frac{d}{ds}\big|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=0$ for every such $h$.

(ii) [Particle sector] For a prescribed external four-potential $A_\mu$ on a
neighbourhood of the image of a $C^2$ future timelike massive worldline $X$,
the motion is dynamically admissible exactly when $X$ is stationary for the
particle functional $S_{\rm pt}$ of clause (c) of that definition under all
fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variations.

This is an adopted assumption of the model, not a theorem, not a derivation
from the remaining postulates and not an empirical result. It asserts
stationarity only: it does not assert that a stationary configuration is a
local or global minimum, that stationary configurations exist or are unique,
that the action functional is uniquely determined or forced by symmetry, that
no other action formulation is possible, or that the two sectors can be
coupled into a single well-posed action for singular sources. No Noether
theorem, no symmetry-to-conservation machinery and no matter dynamics beyond
the prescribed potential are assumed.

The conditional deductions of this pair are: on the declared smooth classes,
(i) is equivalent to the inhomogeneous tensor field equation
$\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ and, for potential-represented fields, to
the smooth-branch Maxwell equations, and (ii) is equivalent to the framework's
adopted four-force equation $m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$; both deductions are
recorded separately on this page and in
[[pthm-em-action-maxwell-variation]] and
[[pthm-em-particle-action-coupling]], and this postulate asserts neither.

configuration space $\mathcal C$ on the spacetime and bundle sector of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]], and a real differentiable functional
$S_m[g,A,\Psi]$ on its declared domain, where $\Psi\in\mathcal C$ and $A$ is a

compact variation class must be specified for the chosen matter model. The
functional is required to be invariant under compactly supported gauge
transformations and orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms, with the
connection and matter fields transported together.

Adopt matter-field stationarity as part of this selected model:
$\delta_\Psi S_m=0$ for every admissible compactly supported matter variation.
For compactly supported inverse-metric variations $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$ and
fixed-sector compact connection variations $\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$, require the
remaining first variation to have the form

$$\delta S_m=-\frac1{2c}\int_M T^m_{ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g +\frac1c\int_M j^a\alpha_a\,\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $T^m$ is a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, the Hilbert
stress-energy tensor in the convention of
[[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]], and $j$ is a smooth vector current.
The normalization, connection variation, and invariance hypotheses are the
formulation interface used by [[lem-emg-matter-noether-exchange]]; that
conditional mathematical result does not assert that such an action exists
for arbitrary proposed matter.

This postulate selects a differentiable action branch and its variation
conventions. It does not determine a unique action, assert a local or global
solution of its Euler–Lagrange equations, extend the model to singular sources,
or establish empirical validity. The separate equation-based model does not
depend on this action assumption.

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla^g_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

This is the selected smooth vacuum constitutive law. The first equation is the homogeneous field equation; the second is the sourced field equation with the sign fixed by $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $j=(c\rho,J)$ in a positively oriented inertial tetrad. No global potential is assumed: although $F=dA$ implies $dF=0$ when a smooth potential exists, the postulate applies to the two-form itself and does not assert that such an $A$ exists globally.

The postulate adopts one curved-spacetime continuation as a physical model assumption. The flat Minkowski and special-relativity suppliers [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], and [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]] fix the inherited SI, inertial, and flat-limit conventions; they do not impose a globally flat metric on $M$ or deduce this curved field law. General-relativity sources describe covariant Maxwell formulations in their own unit and sign conventions; those treatments motivate the chosen formulation but neither mathematical structure nor source authority proves that this is nature's law. No empirical result is adopted here.

The model has no magnetic-charge term and no material excitation pair such as $D,H$. It applies only to smooth $F$ and $j$ on the stated domain; point and sheet sources, distribution-valued fields, and products of distributions require separate definitions and are outside this postulate.

configuration space $\mathcal C$ on the spacetime and bundle sector of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]], and a real differentiable functional
$S_m[g,A,\Psi]$ on its declared domain, where $\Psi\in\mathcal C$ and $A$ is a
connection on the fixed smooth bundle. The field class, transition data and
compact variation class must be specified for the chosen matter model. The
functional is required to be invariant under compactly supported gauge
transformations and orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms, with the
connection and matter fields transported together.

Adopt SI units and the following model-local quantity roles. Here the selected Einstein–Maxwell framework combines the stated Lorentzian geometry with a classical electromagnetic two-form and current; this definition itself supplies no gravitational equation, matter action, or empirical claim. A primitive is an input or independent field variable of this formulation; a derived quantity is fixed by a stated construction from its inputs. Neither label is universal across physical theories, and unit choice alone does not determine it.

The spacetime data are a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless four-manifold $M$, a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a smooth time-orientation field, and an independent orientation, exactly as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The metric, its time orientation, and the manifold orientation are separate data. An observer at $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth observer congruence is a smooth field of such vectors. A local tetrad is a smooth basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; an observer congruence, a coordinate chart, and a tetrad are different objects. Tetrads and observer fields need only exist locally; this definition assumes no global inertial chart, global tetrad, or hypersurface-orthogonal congruence.

The electromagnetic field-strength variable $F$ is a smooth real two-form, hence an alternating covariant tensor of type $(0,2)$, on an open subset of $M$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. It is primitive in this formulation. For an observer congruence $n$, its electric and magnetic observer covectors are derived by

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $\star_g$ is the unique Hodge map characterized pointwise by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, using the metric and independent orientation, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. The elementary charge $e$ is exactly $1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$. These unit definitions do not imply that charge is quantized. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
